newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia c.bank says unhappy with rupiah on FINEX.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia c.bank says unhappy with rupiah on FINEX.

text.p: Indonesian central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Friday he was unhappy with the listing of the rupiah in a futures contract to be launched by FINEX, the financial products division of the New York Cotton Exchange.
"National currency denominated papers floating abroad actually means internationalising of your currency," Djiwandono said in an interview with Reuters.
"The implication is that you don't have any leverage in your authority...because it's outside your jurisdiction," he said. "I don't like it, to put it mildly."
Djiwandono said the central bank, Bank Indonesia, would then be unable to control fluctuations in the currency.
"We cannot do anything but we have to (accept) the impications," he said. "Many times there are negative implications."
FINEX officials have said they tentatively plan to launch the U.S. dollar/rupiah contract on June 26. It also plans to launch similar contracts on the Malaysian ringgit and the Thai baht.
Djiwandono said he would be happy if FINEX excluded the rupiah from its futures contracts. He acknowledged, however, that the central bank had no jurisdiction in the matter.

But the New York Cotton Exchange has excluded the Singapore dollar from the contracts after the country's monetary authority said it was concerned about any trading in the Singapore dollar that could destabilise the market.
